items.title: Mozambique: Mozal and Gapi-SI reinforce funding for entrepreneurship
items.summary: Mozal and Gapi reaffirmed their commitment to financing entrepreneurship and the development of small businesses by delivering 20 financing checks and four grant checks, totalling approximately 10.3 million meticais, to entrepreneurs in the municipalities of Boane and Matola, within the scope of the Nhluvuko Project The fourth check delivery ceremony of the project represents another step in the joint efforts of Mozal and Gapi-SI to expand access to financing, strengthen micro and small businesses, and promote job creation, with particular attention to the economic participation of young people and women Launched in 2023, Nhluvuko is the result of a partnership between Mozal, Gapi-SI, and the Government, and was designed to address one of the main challenges faced by small entrepreneurs: access to adequate financial resources to start, consolidate, and expand their businesses.

items.title: Mozambique: Loveira attends V20 Ministerial Dialogue in Bangkok on sidelines of IMF, World Bank meetings
items.summary: The V20 operates in partnership with the Climate Vulnerable Forum (CVF). The meeting, titled “Development and Delivery in a Multipolar World”, is taking place on the sidelines of the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group Against a backdrop of increasingly frequent and intense climate shocks, the V20 meeting focuses on the challenges associated with mobilising the financial resources needed to support economic development, industrialisation and the strengthening of resilience in developing countries vulnerable to the effects of climate change In this context, finance ministers are seeking not only to increase the volume of available financing, but also to improve the mechanisms through which it is mobilised and deployed.

items.title: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
items.summary: Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros Hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight, according to one supermarket chain affected The chief executive of Coopérative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand were affected, with a spokesman saying that another 100 shops were urgently disconnected from the internet to prevent the same thing happening to them Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely Normally, supermarket freezers go through a short period of defrosting overnight, in which…

items.title: UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers The British government has accused Iran of involvement in a security alert outside a UK/US airbase in southern England last month , summoning the ambassador and announcing sanctions against two individuals Five British nationals were arrested in the vicinity of the RAF Fairford airbase on September 27 on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses.

items.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
items.summary: File photo of gold prospectors in northern Sudan At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining site in Red Sea state on Saturday Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region "The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday.
